chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan and Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that they said:

When a man makes a solemn oath not to approach his wife, she has no say and no right during the four months, and there is no sin upon him in refraining from her during the four months. So if the four months pass before he touches her, and she is silent and pleased, then he is in a state of solution and leeway.

So if she raises her matter, it is said to him: either you return (to intimacy) and touch her, or you divorce her. And the decisive divorce is that he keeps her away. So when she menstruates and becomes pure, he divorces her, and he is more rightful in revoking her as long as three menstrual periods do not pass.
This is the solemn oath (Ila') which Allah, Blessed and High, revealed in His Book, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Solemn oath of abstention from marital intimacy
key_terms.رَجْعَة: Revocation of divorce (taking the wife back during the waiting period)
key_terms.قُرُوء: Menstrual periods (used to count the duration for divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal procedure and timeline for Ila (solemn oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential mechanics of 'Ila', a solemn oath of abstention, by distinguishing between the husband's initial four-month grace period and the subsequent phase where the wife gains the agency to initiate separation. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the husband's obligation to either resume intimacy or effect a decisive divorce (Talaq) after the wife's third purification, ensuring her rights are protected against prolonged indefinite waiting. The text explicitly links this legal framework to the Quranic revelation and the Sunnah of the Prophet, grounding the procedural details in divine authority.
